source.label: existing nationwide completed data.sqlite
source.method: Source reader reports plus current file size/mtime_ns; no full-file cryptographic hash was taken.

scope.method: Read-only existing nationwide DB analysis plus fixed-profile SDK PNG rendering.
scope.profile: osm-like-v1: roads/buildings/labels on, Japanese priority, contours/hillshade off
limitations: Regional anchors, zoom-axis samples and density-selected stress tiles are not every region/zoom combination or every tile up to zoom 22.
Database-wide maxima and conservative high-zoom candidate bounds are separated from sampled rendering outcomes.
Successful SDK times above 60 seconds are reference warnings, not measured HTTP outcomes; queueing/concurrency/cold cache may change HTTP latency.
Rendering work, polygon crossings and glyph limits require real rendering; candidate-count safety alone does not prove their safety.
Source size/mtime equality is not a full-file cryptographic integrity proof.

region_totals_note: One tile can represent several regions; region counts are not disjoint.
latest_result_rule: Last complete record per tile, in base-results then extra-results file order; all-attempt failure counts are retained separately.

nationwide_bound_evidence.evidence_type: DB-wide numeric scans/conservative bounds, not exhaustive PNG generation
nationwide_bound_evidence.high_zoom_density_sampling_scope: R-tree density beam search within each root branch, followed by exact z14 candidate counts; not an exhaustive z14 ranking

road_name_proof_and_limitations.database_rows: Every one of 10,668,302 road R-tree rows and 529,313 name R-tree rows was processed once; source opened mode=ro&immutable=1 and query_only.
road_name_proof_and_limitations.road_0_5: The renderer returns no road candidates below zoom 6.
road_name_proof_and_limitations.road_6_9: Exact full coverage of all tile coordinates intersecting source bounds plus query margin; Style::visible includes one-zoom link delay.
road_name_proof_and_limitations.road_10_22: All road categories at zoom 10 give a conservative upper bound for each finer tile: every fine query rectangle is inside its zoom-10 parent query rectangle. Maximum 368,934 < 1,000,000.
road_name_proof_and_limitations.names_0_4: No category is visible below zoom 5.
road_name_proof_and_limitations.names_5_13: Exact full candidate count and in-memory byte accounting on all source-covered tiles; category minimum zoom and fixed-cell label query bounds included.
road_name_proof_and_limitations.names_14_22: All 24 categories at zoom 14 bound every finer tile, as each fine label query is inside its parent label query. Maximum 5,307 candidates / 1,001,047 bytes.
road_name_proof_and_limitations.single_tile_name_query: At 256px, label_query_bounds is [(x-2)/2^z,(x+3)/2^z] times the same y bounds, clamped to 0..1. Outward-rounded SQLite R-tree coordinates are used.
road_name_proof_and_limitations.limits_accounted: Road candidate keys <=1,000,000; label candidates <=100,000; names bytes+112 bytes per LabelCandidate <=16MiB. sizeof values independently confirmed by parent Rust SDK runner.
road_name_proof_and_limitations.limitations: This is exhaustive candidate-count/byte accounting with conservative high-zoom bounds, not exhaustive PNG rendering. It does not prove every tile avoids rendering work/time/crossing limits or name glyph/shape limits; these require SDK stress rendering. The MAX_LAYOUTS count is separately bounded by layout_count_bound.

label_layout_count_bound.scope: All 529313 stored anchors and z0..22, 256x256 single-tile rendering; glyph count/shape errors are separate.

single_road_geometry_bound.scope: One metadata-only aggregate over all base features; no geometry_lod table scan.
single_road_geometry_bound.lod_inference: Importer constructs each LOD by simplifying base road vertices, preserving a subset of input vertices. LOD count cannot exceed base count under that import rule; this is a rule-based bound, not a readback audit of all LOD rows.

low_zoom_query_plan_evidence.method: sqlite_master metadata and EXPLAIN only; no feature scan
findings: All five passes scan the matching R-tree range, seek each feature row by primary key, and use a temporary B-tree for ordering.
There is no min_zoom/kind-first covering index, so invisible buildings still cause feature-row lookups before the min_zoom/pass filter.
For world/near-world low zoom ranges, the R-tree range contains almost all geometries; sorting is blocking, so the first visible feature is not returned until the scan completes.

The existing UNIQUE(osm_type,osm_id,role,kind) index supports an osm_type=3 prefix search for current importer landmask rows, but this cannot be assumed for arbitrary valid completed datasets without a compatibility strategy.
